claims.claim: The Renaissance was a European revival of interest in classical Greek and Roman learning and art, running roughly from the 14th to the 17th century and beginning in the Italian city-states, especially Florence.

Humanism, the intellectual core of the Renaissance, renewed interest in the classical world and focused on human potential and the studia humanitatis (grammar, rhetoric, history, poetry, moral philosophy), studying secular subjects alongside religious ones rather than replacing religion.
Petrarch (1304-1374) is often called the father of humanism and recovered lost ancient manuscripts.
Linear perspective was demonstrated by Brunelleschi around 1420 and codified by Leon Battista Alberti in his treatise On Painting (Della Pittura) in 1435.
The High Renaissance is associated with Leonardo da Vinci (1452-1519), Michelangelo (1475-1564), and Raphael (1483-1520).
Wealthy patrons, notably the Medici of Florence (e.g., Cosimo and Lorenzo de' Medici), funded artists, scholars, and buildings and thereby shaped Renaissance culture.

Johannes Gutenberg developed a practical movable-type printing press in Europe around 1440 (Mainz), printing his Bible c. 1455, which greatly accelerated the reproduction and spread of texts and ideas compared with hand-copying.
Movable type existed earlier in East Asia; Gutenberg's contribution was a workable movable-type press suited to Europe, not the invention of printing itself.

Much classical knowledge re-entered western Europe through Islamic scholars (who translated Greek works into Arabic from the 8th-9th centuries and advanced them) and via later Latin translations at centers such as Toledo (12th-13th c.), and through Byzantine/Greek scholars who carried manuscripts west, especially after Constantinople fell in 1453.
The Renaissance was largely an elite, urban movement; most Europeans were rural, poor, and often illiterate, and their daily lives changed little during the period.

conflictingEvidence.issue: Exact start/end dates of the Renaissance
positions: Some scholars date the Italian Renaissance from the 14th century (Petrarch)
Others emphasize a 15th-16th century flowering; northern Renaissance extends into the 17th century
conflictingEvidence.resolution: Presented as an approximate span (roughly 14th-17th century), with the movement beginning in 14th-century Italy and maturing in the 15th-16th centuries. Framed as a hindsight label, not a fixed program.

positions: c. 1450-1455 for refined operation and the Gutenberg Bible
conflictingEvidence.resolution: Stated as 'around 1440' for the press and 'about 1455' for the Bible, consistent with Britannica.

sourceRecords.title: Johannes Gutenberg
sourceRecords.notes: Reference-only cross-check for printing dates. Confirms Gutenberg designed and built the first known mechanized (movable-type) printing press in Europe, with development around 1440 in Mainz, refinement by 1450, and the Gutenberg Bible printed in 1455. Used per source-map caution that Britannica is a cross-check, never a sole source; the printing claims are corroborated by OpenStax.
